source.title: Vanishing Nodes: Another Phenomenon That Makes Training Deep Neural Networks Difficult

record.tranche_reason: Tests how initialization and depth affect training success in fully connected MNIST networks, using different tasks and measures from the initialization and trainable-depth claims.
record.gate_note: Directly tests V4. It reports MNIST training outcomes under initialization, depth, and learning-rate conditions. It does not test the CIFAR-specific near-zero-error claim in V1: the experiments use MNIST and define success as accuracy above 90%, not near-zero training error. Learning-rate results do not test V5's stability-threshold or catapult claims. Table 2 aggregates outcomes by optimizer, activation, and initialization; Table 3 reports specific depths and outcomes. Figure 6 has no extractable numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 in a new setting: fully connected MNIST networks initialized to preserve signal and gradient scales. It compares training success across initialization, depth and learning rate. Standard initializations sometimes fail, while orthogonal tanh initialization has the highest success probability. Deliberately induced collapse in Section 5 does not independently test naturally arising training difficulty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they attribute training failures to increasing hidden-node correlation and reduced effective representation capacity, even without vanishing or exploding gradient scales, and report that maintaining orthogonal weights eases these failures. Their causal interpretation should remain attributed to them; the observed VNI association alone does not establish causation.
record.recipe_differences: Fully connected tanh or ReLU MNIST networks and simple AND/XOR tasks; compares scaled-Gaussian, orthogonal, rank-bottleneck initialization, and Householder weight parameterization. It does not use the listed CIFAR/ImageNet recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcomes vary with initialization or parameterization, depth, learning rate, activation, and task. The text states that high learning rates can intensify VNI and that failure likelihood is high when depth and learning rate are large.

fits_no_version.finding: Deliberately setting initial VNI near one prevents four-class AND, XOR and MNIST learning, while two-class AND remains learnable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Imposed node correlation can prevent learning despite approximately preserved gradient scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Maintaining orthogonal weights with Householder parameterization succeeds at depths 50, 200 and 500, including 20 successful runs at depth 500 and learning rate 0.01.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Enforcing orthogonality throughout training can prevent failures that remain possible with orthogonal initialization alone.

fits_no_version.finding: Failed runs have VNI concentrated near one, whereas successful runs have lower and more broadly distributed VNI.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final node correlation is associated with training failure in these MNIST experiments.

record.problems: Experiments use MNIST and toy tasks rather than CIFAR benchmarks. Table 1 and Table 3 report categorical outcomes without uncertainty estimates. Figure 6 provides probability plots without extractable values in the supplied text. Table 2 is flattened, so its individual counts cannot be safely mapped to conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6's per-depth and per-learning-rate probability values are figure-only and not stated in the text; no precise values were extracted. Table 2 counts are not assigned to specific optimizer/activation/initialization combinations because the flattened layout does not securely support that mapping.

untested.parts: CIFAR convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, and zero or near-zero training classification error.
ReLU teacher-student local minima and adding one or two student neurons.
Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity shortcuts, longer training, and Fixup.
Direct orthogonal-versus-Gaussian learning-speed comparisons at matched variance; 10,000-layer convolutional training. The main MNIST outcome is crossing 90% training accuracy within 100 epochs.
Initial linearized stability thresholds, catapult recovery, curvature trajectories and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup.

missing.what: Successful and failed trained networks both have the paper's gradient-scale diagnostic near one. This is needed to assess the qualification that norm preservation alone does not ensure trainability.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Section 5 uses testing accuracy, while Section 6 uses training accuracy. Figure 6's omitted numerical probabilities and Table 2's unresolved count mapping were already declared in rows_left_out. Deliberately induced collapse and maintained-orthogonality interventions are separated from initialization-only verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional models, corrupted or random labels, and near-zero training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks and shortcut connections.

Activation-matched initialization on the named CIFAR/ImageNet models; comparisons of orthogonal and Gaussian weights at the same variance in very deep tanh networks; 10,000-layer convolutional training. The study tests fully connected MNIST networks and simple toy tasks.
Stability-limit overshoot, curvature drop, edge-of-stability sharpness, and the stated full-batch squared-loss conditions.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup residual networks.
